title: Hotend heating failed
shortDescription: Hotend did not reach target temperature in time.
fullDescription:
Anycubic Kobra series uses Marlin-based firmware with thermal runaway protection. A heating error appears when the hotend heat-up rate is too slow — usually from a loose heater cartridge, missing silicone sock, or failing thermistor.

Check hardware before retrying — the firmware disables heating until reset.

fixSteps.title: Install silicone sock
fixSteps.instruction: Fit a sock over the heater block.

fixSteps.title: Tighten heater screw
fixSteps.instruction: With the hotend cold, tighten the heater cartridge setscrew.

whenToCallPro: If heater keeps failing after replacement.

faq.q: How to reset after heating error?

title: First layer not sticking to PEI plate
shortDescription: Print peels off during first layer.
fullDescription:
Anycubic PEI plates work best when clean and at the right Z offset. Fingerprints or dust cause adhesion failure on the first layer.

Clean with IPA and re-run auto bed leveling.

fixSteps.title: Clean plate
fixSteps.instruction: Wipe with IPA and a microfiber cloth.

faq.a: Not for PLA/PETG on clean PEI.

title: Resin leaked from vat
shortDescription: Resin leaked onto the LCD screen or chassis.
fullDescription:
Resin printers can leak if the FEP film is damaged or the vat screws are not torqued evenly. Leaked resin onto the LCD cures on the screen and may ruin it.

Immediately power off and clean with IPA and paper towels. Wear gloves.

fixSteps.title: Power off and clean
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug, wear gloves, clean with IPA. Do NOT cure resin on LCD.

fixSteps.title: Replace FEP
fixSteps.instruction: Remove vat, unscrew frame, replace FEP film, re-tension evenly.

whenToCallPro: If LCD is cured with resin.
videoSearchQuery: Anycubic Photon resin leak FEP replacement

faq.q: Is cured resin on LCD fixable?

title: Z-axis motor stalled
shortDescription: Z motor cannot move due to binding or obstruction.
fullDescription: Z stalls happen when the lead screw is dry or misaligned. On resin printers the bed is heavy so any binding becomes obvious. Lubricate and align.

fixSteps.title: Lubricate lead screw
fixSteps.instruction: Apply PTFE grease along the full length.

fixSteps.title: Align Z bracket
fixSteps.instruction: Loosen and retighten the Z bracket with the bed at mid-travel.

title: Stepper motor skipping steps
shortDescription: X or Y motor skipping steps during print.
fullDescription: Skipping is caused by too-tight belts, dry rods, or driver overcurrent. Results in layer shift. Reduce speed and acceleration first to confirm mechanical vs electrical cause.

fixSteps.title: Reduce speed
fixSteps.instruction: Drop print speed to 50mm/s to confirm the issue.

fixSteps.title: Lubricate rods
fixSteps.instruction: Apply light machine oil to all smooth rods.

faq.a: Yes — that's the driver missing a step.

title: Masking LCD error
shortDescription: Resin printer's masking LCD shows lines or won't display.
fullDescription: The masking LCD on resin printers is a consumable. After ~1000 hours of exposure it dims or develops dead pixels. Resin leaks also damage it. Replacement is user-serviceable on most Anycubic models.

fixSteps.title: Run LCD test
fixSteps.instruction: Menu → Tools → LCD test pattern — look for dead zones.

fixSteps.title: Replace LCD
fixSteps.instruction: Order correct LCD for your model and follow the service guide.

whenToCallPro: If you haven't opened the printer before.

faq.q: How long does an LCD last?

title: UV LED module not working
shortDescription: Resin printer's UV array is not emitting light.
fullDescription: The UV LED array sits below the masking LCD. If it fails, prints do not cure even though the LCD shows images. Cable, fan, and LED driver failures are the common causes.

fixSteps.title: Check UV fan
fixSteps.instruction: Power on and listen for the UV fan — it must run during exposure.

fixSteps.title: Inspect UV module cable
fixSteps.instruction: Open base and reseat UV module power cable.

whenToCallPro: If the UV driver on the mainboard is damaged.
videoSearchQuery: Anycubic Photon UV LED not working

title: Auto bed leveling failed
shortDescription: Leveling probe failed during the mesh routine.
fullDescription:
Anycubic Kobra uses LeviQ strain-gauge auto leveling. Failures come from a dirty nozzle tip, a warped plate, or a loose build plate magnet.

Wipe the nozzle clean before each leveling cycle.

fixSteps.title: Clean nozzle
fixSteps.instruction: With hotend at 200°C, wipe nozzle tip with brass brush.

fixSteps.title: Flatten plate
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure PEI plate is fully seated on the magnet.

faq.a: After changing plates or moving printer.

title: Cannot read print file
shortDescription: Printer cannot open or parse the selected file.
fullDescription: File read errors happen from exFAT cards, oversized USB drives, corrupted downloads, or filenames with special characters. Use FAT32, short filenames.

causes.cause: USB formatted exFAT instead of FAT32

fixSteps.title: Rename file
fixSteps.instruction: Use only letters, numbers, and dashes in filename.

title: Slicer failed to generate gcode
shortDescription: Anycubic Slicer / Photon Workshop failed to export a valid file.
fullDescription: Slicer errors are usually model issues: non-manifold mesh, intersecting shells, or zero-thickness walls. Repair in Meshmixer or use slicer's auto-repair.

fixSteps.title: Auto-repair model
fixSteps.instruction: Use slicer auto-repair or Meshmixer's Inspector.

fixSteps.title: Reset slicer profile
fixSteps.instruction: Delete printer profile and re-add from defaults.

faq.a: Yes for FDM — import the Anycubic profile.
